title: Sega GT 2002
subtitle: A racing career begins with an affordable car

body: Sega GT 2002 is Wow Entertainment's Xbox racing simulation, released in North America on 3 September 2002. The player begins a career with a limited budget, buys a car and enters events to earn the money needed for improvements or another vehicle. Timed licence laps provide milestones without splitting driving into a long sequence of separate manoeuvre tests. The game connects the immediate lap to a developing garage, making each race useful as both a driving challenge and an opportunity to prepare the vehicle that will enter the next event.

A damage meter records contact during a race, reducing the prize money when the car has been knocked around. Finishing without damage can instead produce a cash bonus. Although the damage does not change handling, it affects the career beyond the finishing position, giving the player another reason to avoid an untidy pass. Chronicle Mode offers a different progression through historic cars from the 1960s and early 1970s. Improving those machines and racing newer opposition connects the development of a single car to the broader changes represented by the collection.

The sequel followed the Dreamcast's Sega GT and later reached many Xbox owners through a bundled disc shared with Jet Set Radio Future. Quick Battle, Time Attack and replay tools offered alternatives to the career, while Sega GT Online subsequently expanded the concept with additional cars and network play. Reviews were generally favourable. Sega GT 2002 belongs to the period when Sega's console franchises were establishing themselves on other manufacturers' hardware, carrying a recognisable garage-building racing structure into an Xbox catalogue increasingly associated with driving games of its own.
